key_insight: LiL-Q replaces nonconvex PINN training with a convex sequence of linear least-squares solves after quasilinearizing the nonlinear PDE, making physics-informed learning more stable and directly solvable.
engineering_relevance: The approach can improve reliability and parameter efficiency for solving nonlinear PDEs in scientific computing, especially when fast convergence and deterministic optimization are important.
method: Bellman-Kalaba quasilinearization turns each nonlinear PDE into a linear subproblem.
Each subproblem is discretized on a Linear-in-Learnables trial space and solved by QR-based least squares.
Trial spaces include random features, spectral polynomials, and trigonometric expansions implemented as PINNs.
evidence_signal: Across seven benchmarks spanning scalar PDEs, coupled systems, and Darcy flow, LiL-Q typically converged in single-digit outer iterations and matched or exceeded published PINNs on Navier-Stokes with up to two orders of magnitude fewer trainable parameters.
watch_item: Convergence is local and depends on a smallness condition, so performance may degrade if the initial guess or problem nonlinearity falls outside the proven regime.
paper_title: A Convex Quasilinearization Method for Solving Nonlinear PDEs with Physics-Informed Neural Networks
